rule: Every example is pinned to the exact language authority. Compiler-evidence examples are derived from executed current-authority fixtures, but the live endpoint remains the authority for the current run. Law projections teach admitted meaning without claiming parser, lowering, execution, or performance support.

capabilities.compiler-evidence: source derived from an executed current-authority fixture; analyze, run, and lower remain live observations
capabilities.law-projection: admitted language meaning; implementation support is intentionally not claimed

examples.title: existential relation without loop ceremony
examples.summary: Ask one semantic question of a fixed-shape subject, then inspect the application, subject, operand, result, demand, and selected realization.
examples.source:
# any is one relation identity over the collection subject
xs: [3]i64 = {3, 5, 8}
hit = xs:any((x) x % 2 == 0)
print(hit)
meaning: existential demand remains visible before realization

examples.title: world-backed place and absence semantics
examples.summary: Update an exact environment place, read it through the same world relation, and preserve the distinction between an empty value and absence.
examples.source:
# environment is a world-backed place; the empty value remains present
env("IDOLHOME") = "ready"
value = env("IDOLHOME") or "absent"
print(value)
meaning: env is reached from the current world
the indexed write and read share one place identity
authority is separate from the value spelling
absence and the empty value remain different facts

examples.title: direct relation and result chaining
examples.summary: A sequence of subject-oriented applications keeps every occurrence distinct while the demanded result supplies the next exact subject.
meaning: ordinary relation applications share one application algebra
each exact demanded result supplies the next semantic subject
the tail expression supplies the demanded result
no pipeline operator or pipeline object exists
refuses: first-result fallback when a pack is ambiguous

examples.title: subject and projection specialization
examples.summary: One relation identity is qualified by a subject constraint and a stable projection fact; ordinary payload remains in the application pack.
examples.source:
# kg is a stable relation projection; factor is ordinary payload
body:weight(kg) = (factor)
    :mass()
        * factor

examples.title: computed and static projection
examples.summary: Computed indexing and one static named projection remain distinct from ordinary and subject-oriented application.
examples.source:
value = table[key]
table[key] = replacement
encoded = codec.encode(source)
meaning: neither face is subject-oriented relation application
